newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin heart pain "completely gone" - Kremlin.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin heart pain "completely gone" - Kremlin.

text.p: The pain around Boris Yeltsin's heart, which troubled the Russian president before his quintuple bypass operation last week, is now "completely gone", a Kremlin spokesman said on Wednesday, quoting doctors.

A routine health bulletin signed by chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov said Yeltsin, who had surgery on November 5, was in a stable condition. His blood pressure was 110/70 with a steady pulse of 88. His temperature was normal.
On Tuesday, Kremlin aides said Yeltsin, 65, would broadcast to the nation "in the next few days".

The president is expected to move from the Central Clinical Hospital to the state sanatorium at Barvikha, near Moscow, in about a week. He is said to be gradually taking up his work and doctors say he could be back in the Kremlin around new year.
